metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson Gets Outsnapped as Tennessee's Rotation Shifts
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson logged 38 offensive snaps (60%) in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns while Carnell Tate and Elic Ayomanor each played 56 snaps and drew seven targets. Robinson can be dropped in 10-team leagues and is expendable in most 12-team formats, particularly outside full PPR, while managers in 14-team PPR leagues can retain him as receiving depth, although Tennessee's Week 9 bye makes that decision less appealing. He also failed to capitalize on Calvin Ridley's (hip) absence in the loss, catching four of six targets for just seven yards. His snap share has fallen from 75% in Week 5, and he has converted 13 targets into just seven receptions for 29 yards over his past two appearances. His 43 targets through seven games suggest he remains involved in the offense, but those opportunities have yielded only 205 yards at 7.1 yards per reception.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson held to seven yards in Week 7
metadata.description: Wan'Dale Robinson caught four of his six targets for seven yards in a 27-24 loss to the Browns in Week 7.
metadata.analysis: Robinson was held to just 1.8 yards per carry by a tough Cleveland secondary. The veteran wideout has topped 50 receiving yards just twice in seven contests this season. Robinson will be a WR4 in fantasy heading into Week 8 against the Bengals.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson - Minimal production in loss
metadata.description: Robinson caught four of seven targets for seven yards during Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
metadata.analysis: Robinson garnered exactly seven targets for the third straight week, but his seven receiving yards were a new season low for the wideout. Robinson is pretty much limited to short and intermediate routes, and as a result, he has a rather low floor from a fantasy perspective. On the year, the wide receiver has reeled in 29 of 44 targets for 205 yards and two touchdowns over seven contests so far.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson Remains a Low-Floor PPR Flex Option
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson remains in the flex conversation for Sunday's meeting with the visiting Cleveland Browns and offers a solid floor for fantasy managers in need of stability. Robinson has cleared only 70% of Tennessee's snaps in two games this season, though he's stayed steadily involved in the team's attack, commanding five or more targets in all but one outing. While he doesn't project to be a huge help outside of PPR formats, the former New York Giant could see a minor increase in production for this Sunday's matchup with the Browns. Fellow wideout Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable to play, which should force Robinson into a slightly larger snap share. Through six weeks, Robinson ranks as the clear second on the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards, while pacing Tennessee's pass catchers with two touchdowns.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson Looking to Bounce Back
metadata.description: It was a slow week for Tennessee Titans wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson in Week 6, as he hauled in just three of seven targets for 22 yards during a win over the Indianapolis Colts. This week, Robinson is hoping to rebound, but may find it difficult to do so as he and the Titans go up against a strong Cleveland Browns pass defense that has recorded the 10th-best passing EPA per play allowed (-0.10) in the NFL, according to Next Gen Stats. The Browns gave up just 10 receptions for 106 yards to Baltimore Ravens wide receivers a week ago. Fellow Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley did not practice on Thursday or Friday and has been marked questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, per the Titans injury report. If Ridley cannot play, that could mean more targets for Robinson.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson snags three passes in win
metadata.description: Wan'Dale Robinson caught three of seven targets for 22 yards in the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Robinson and Carnell Tate were the only pass catchers to catch more than one pass from Cam Ward on Sunday, and also the only two to go over 10 yards. Robinson has had some usable performances this year, but they seem to come on an every-other-week basis.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson - Held to two catches in win
metadata.description: Robinson caught three of seven targets for 22 yards during Sunday's 26-20 win over the Colts.
metadata.analysis: Robinson finished tied for the team lead in targets with fellow wideout Carnell Tate, but he finished with 22 or fewer receiving yards for the second time in three weeks and the third time overall this season. The wide receiver, along with the rest of Tennessee's offense, is incredibly inconsistent, but he has seen at least five targets in four straight games.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson an Excellent Play Off Waivers
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson has been productive recently and will look to continue that trend on the road against the Indianapolis Colts. Robinson's 2026 numbers won't jump off the page, but he's still provided value, even in the league's worst scoring offense. Aside from a one-catch dud in Week 2, the fifth-year pro has been solid, collecting at least five targets in all but one appearance and five or more receptions in three. Robinson's outlook also improves in Week 6 with a tantalizing matchup against a sieve-like Colts pass defense. Over six weeks, Indianapolis ranks fifth in passing yards allowed per game (254) and sixth in points allowed per game (27.6). A sub-optimal offensive line and erratic play from quarterback Cam Ward work against him, but the Kentucky native is well-positioned to produce ahead of the divisional clash.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson leads Titans in receiving Sunday
metadata.description: Wan'Dale Robinson caught 6-of-7 targets for 53 yards in the Titans 26-3 loss against the Texans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Robinson posted his third game with 50 yards on the season. He remains a WR3/ flex play next week against the Colts.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson - Leading receiver in loss to Houston
metadata.description: Robinson caught six of seven targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 26-3 loss to the Texans.
metadata.analysis: The 53 yards led the Titans on the afternoon, while the target and catch volume led the team's wide receivers, although running back Tyjae Spears posted a 9-28-0 line on nine targets. Robinson's strength on short routes out of the slot is matching well with Cam Ward's reluctance to stretch the field, and through five games for Tennessee the veteran wideout has a 22-176-2 line on 30 targets. He'll look to keep stacking PPR value in a Week 6 clash with the Colts.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson Trending Up After Scoring in Back-to-Back Games
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson should be more popular off the waiver wire this week after finding the end zone for a second straight game in Sunday's 24-18 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4. Robinson was out-snapped by rookie Carnell Tate 54 to 43 in the game and caught only three passes for 19 yards, but he found the end zone for the second straight week after his seven-catch, 57-yard, one-touchdown performance in the Week 3 loss to the New York Giants. The 25-year-old's touchdown on Sunday came with just over a minute left in regulation. He has not been the target hog that he was the last few years with the Giants, as Robinson has 16 catches on 23 targets for 123 yards and two touchdowns in his first four games with Tennessee. Still, Robinson can be useful as wide receiver depth for fantasy managers, especially if he can continue to develop chemistry with young quarterback Cam Ward. He could be a nice flex play at wideout for the Titans' upcoming matchup this Sunday against the winless Houston Texans.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson - Notches another touchdown in Week 4
metadata.description: Robinson caught three of five targets for 19 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 24-18 loss to the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: Robinson was able to find paydirt for the second straight week, connecting with quarterback Cam Ward for a three-yard touchdown with 1:16 left in regulation. The wide receiver finished second on the team in targets behind rookie first-rounder Carnell Tate (12), and Robinson has now caught 16 of 23 targets for 123 yards and two touchdowns over the first four contests of the 2026 campaign.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson hauls in three passes in Week 4
metadata.description: Wan'Dale Robinson caught 3-of-5 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Titans loss to the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: Robinson caught the lone touchdown pass from Cam Ward against the Ravens, giving Robinson a touchdown in back-to-back games. The 25-year-old will look to continue that streak in Week 5 against the Texans.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson Re-Emerging as a PPR Waiver-Wire Target
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson had his best game of the 2026 season in his team's Week 3 loss to the New York Giants, recording seven catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets. The 25-year-old had gotten off to a slow start to his first season in Tennessee, hauling in just six catches on seven targets across the Titans' first two games. However, Robinson has proven he can be a target and reception machine in the past, recording at least 90 catches and 140 targets in both 2024 and 2025. Particularly with Titans quarterback Cam Ward struggling, Robinson should continue to see plenty of work in the short and intermediate areas of the field. Tennessee's overall offensive struggles limit Robinson's upside, but he profiles as a high-floor PPR wide receiver for fantasy managers to target on the waiver wire.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson finds end zone Sunday
metadata.description: Wan'Dale Robinson caught 7-of-11 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
metadata.analysis: Robinson played well against his former team on Sunday. He led the team in targets and receptions against the Giants, and he also scored the team's only touchdown over the course of the afternoon. Despite the good game, fantasy managers should not consider him a viable option moving forward.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson - Hauls in TD against former team
metadata.description: Robinson caught seven of 11 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the Giants.
metadata.analysis: The wideout got a measure of revenge against his former employer, catching a four-yard strike from Cam Ward late in the fourth quarter to give the Titans a flicker of hope, but the comeback fell short. Robinson led his new team in targets and catches on the day, although Carnell Tate had one more receiving yard. Through his first three games with Tennessee, Robinson's posted a 13-104-1 line on 18 targets heading into a Week 4 road trip to Baltimore.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson's Target Volume Has Dried Up
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson went from six targets in the opener to one against Philadelphia, and that is a rough drop for a player whose fantasy value has always depended on volume. Robinson caught five passes for 38 yards in Week 1, then finished with one catch for nine yards last Sunday. He has six receptions for 47 yards through two games and has yet to score. Rookie Carnell Tate already leads Tennessee with 11 targets, while Robinson sits at seven. That is a very different setup from last season, when Robinson drew 140 targets with the Giants and turned them into 92 catches for 1,014 yards and four touchdowns. Tennessee gave him a four-year, $78 million deal in March, so there is still a substantial investment here. The early usage just has not matched it. Robinson checks in at WR57 in RotoBaller's latest Week 3 rankings. Until Cam Ward starts looking his way more often, Robinson is difficult to trust outside of deeper PPR leagues.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson held to one catch in Week 2
metadata.description: Wan'Dale Robinson caught his lone target for a nine-yard gain in a 24-20 loss to the Eagles in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Robinson was quiet in what was almost an upset win over the Eagles. The Titans only passed for 183 yards in the contest with Elic Ayomanor leading the way. Through two games in Tennessee, Robinson has caught six of his seven targets for 47 scoreless yards. He will need to see more frequent work moving forward to be trustworthy in fantasy. The Titans will face the Giants in Week 3.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson - One catch in Week 2
metadata.description: Robinson caught his only target for nine yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Eagles.
metadata.analysis: Robinson was even more quiet in his second contest with Tennessee after he caught five passes for 38 yards in his lackluster Titans' regular-season debut Week 1 versus the Jets. The wide receiver is coming off of a 2025 campaign during which he notched 1,014 yards and four touchdowns (both career highs) on 92 catches over 16 regular-season contests with the Giants, and he'll have to establish chemistry with new quarterback Cam Ward quickly if he wants to come anywhere close to those numbers. Robinson and the Titans will travel to face the Giants on the road in Week 3.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson Is a Priority PPR Add for Week 2
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson gave fantasy managers a familiar stat line in Sunday's 23-10 loss to the New York Jets, catching five of six targets for 38 yards. It wasn't a big day, but the six targets tied rookie Carnell Tate for the team lead while Cam Ward managed only 140 passing yards. Robinson's value has never depended on piling up deep shots. He caught 92 passes for 1,014 yards and four touchdowns with the Giants last season, then signed with Tennessee and reunited with offensive coordinator Brian Daboll. The Titans also list him as a starter, so there is no role question to solve here. What needs to improve is the offense around him. Tennessee produced only 195 total yards in the opener, and Robinson averaged 7.6 yards per catch. That can make him frustrating outside of full-PPR formats. Still, five catches in a poor offensive showing are enough to keep the floor interesting. If Robinson was left on the waiver wire, he should be a priority add in PPR leagues ahead of Week 2 against Philadelphia, with more value as a steady depth option than a high-ceiling play.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson - Logs five catches in Titans debut
metadata.description: Robinson finished Sunday's Week 1 loss to the Jets with five catches for 38 yards.
metadata.analysis: Tennessee's offense struggled as a whole Sunday, and the addition of Robinson and rookie Carnell Tate to the wideout corps didn't do much to improve QB Cam Ward's performance following a disappointing rookie season. Robinson and Tate both turned six targets into 38 yards, with Robinson logging five catches to Tate's four. As has been the case throughout Robinson's career, he was deployed mostly in short yardage, averaging a meager 7.6 yards per catch. Robinson blossomed with the Giants last year for a career-best 1,014 receiving yards on 92 catches, but he may struggle to reach those marks in 2026 if Ward doesn't show considerable improvement.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robninson goes for 38 yards in Week 1
metadata.description: Wan'Dale Robinson caught five of his six targets for 38 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Robinson tied for the team lead in targets and receiving yards while leading the way with his five catches. The entire Tennessee offense struggled to move the ball in Week 1, which cut into Robinson's final stats. He will look to bounce back as a decent flex option in PPR leagues heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson a High-Floor PPR Flex Play in Week 1
metadata.description: After spending the first four years of his NFL career with the New York Giants, wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson is entering his first season with the Tennessee Titans in 2026. The 25-year-old was paid by Tennessee after putting together a career year with the Giants in 2025, recording 92 catches for 1,014 yards and four touchdowns on 140 targets across 16 games. In Week 1, the Titans will host the New York Jets. New York struggled to defend the pass in 2025, finishing as a bottom-10 unit in terms of yards per pass attempt allowed (7.5). Robinson may not see many chances down the field on Sunday, as the Titans' passing game has questions entering quarterback Cam Ward's second NFL season. Still, Robinson should see steady target volume as a safety blanket for Ward out of the slot. Fantasy managers should not expect high-end production from Robinson, but he profiles as a potential deep-league PPR flex option in Week 1.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson (head) off injury report for Week 1
metadata.description: Wan'Dale Robinson (head) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 1's matchup against the New York Jets.
metadata.analysis: As expected, Robinson's head injury is no longer an issue and he carries no injury designation heading into Week 1. He should be a full go against the Jets and projects to be a worthwhile streaming option in PPR formats.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson - No injury designation
metadata.description: Robinson (head) is not on the Titans' Wednesday injury report.
metadata.analysis: The Titans' big offseason addition at wideout will be good to go for his team debut Sunday, as Robinson carries no injury designation. Both Robinson and rookie Carnell Tate are off the injury report, signaling that Cam Ward will have his top weapons at his disposal as the team starts a new chapter under head coach Robert Saleh.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson Worth Adding Ahead of Week 1
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson enters Week 1 with a chance to be the team's leading receiver in 2026. Last season with the New York Giants, Robinson had a career year, hauling in 92 of 140 targets for 1,014 yards and four touchdowns in 16 games. Robinson cashed out, signing a four-year, $70 million contract with the Titans in free agency. He performed well in training camp, leading the team in targets, and has been a security blanket for second-year quarterback Cam Ward. In Week 1, he faces an ideal matchup against the New York Jets, who allowed the fifth most fantasy points to slot receivers in 2025. While he's a risky start given the team's uncertainty around its passing game, Robinson should be rostered in all formats as we approach the season.

metadata.title: Wan'Dale Robinson a PPR Sleeper with Large Target Share Expected
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson currently has an ADP of 130.8, and he's emerging as a potential sleeper in PPR leagues because of his anticipated role. Robinson is coming off a fantastic season with the Giants, catching 92 of his 140 targets for 1,014 yards and four touchdowns. He's not a major threat for otherworldly yardage or touchdown totals, but he was peppered with targets in New York, and that trend should continue in Tennessee. First of all, the Titans gave him a four-year, $78 million contract, demonstrating a financial commitment to getting him heavily involved, especially as rookie Carnell Tate adjusts to the NFL. Furthermore, Robinson's new offensive coordinator in Tennessee is Brian Daboll, who was the Giants' head coach for the first portion of last season. Assuming Daboll's Titans offense looks similar to his Giants offense, Robinson should continue to fetch a very high target share, making him a very appealing target in PPR leagues, especially at his current ADP. Robinson has top-25 receiver upside after finishing as the WR14 last year, yet he's being drafted as the WR46 this year. That's a major discrepancy and could be an opportunity for managers to get a steal in the 10th round of fantasy drafts.
